paragraphs: Morning light lies across the carpet in long, flattering stripes. The room is less a bedroom than a dressing room that happens to contain a bed.
She bends to zip the overnight bag, giving everyone a view of the impossible bow sculpted on the back of her pantyhose.
The sedan sits low and patient on the hot asphalt, like a dog that knows it is about to be asked for something unreasonable.
A low gurgle rolls through the car. The seatbelt retracts itself with a polite whizz, all the way to the pillar.
A tidy little house with a wind chime and a hose coiled like a sleeping snake. MA MA LING stands on the porch.
Rainee-Peter unfolds from the passenger seat in stages, like a lawn chair. Ma Ma Ling watches without blinking.
She hits send. Considers. Adds a heart. Deletes the heart. Adds it back.
Francine loops an arm around Rainee's waist, as far as her arms can reach. Rainee's hips brush both sides of the runner.
